citations.anchor: applies the plugins the host built, against the configured URL
citations.why: The spec mocks the `@orthacms/cli` module and asserts the Nx db-migrate executor calls `applyPluginMigrations(plugins, url)`; a second migration implementation inside @orthacms/nx would leave the mock uncalled and fail it. (The generated-app half — migrateCommand calling the same export — is not itself pinned by a test.)

citations.anchor: applies plugins in exactly the order the host listed them
citations.why: Asserts the sequence of `migrationsTable` values passed to drizzle's migrate() equals the host's list order exactly, so any sorting or reordering fails it.

citations.anchor: opens no connection when no plugin ships migrations
citations.why: Asserts the pg Pool constructor and migrate() are never called for a plugin list where nobody declares a migrations descriptor — the 'no connection is opened' clause.

citations.anchor: applies plugins in exactly the order the host listed them
citations.why: The same list contains a descriptor-less plugin (`{ name: 'mcp' }`) and the expected table sequence omits it — the 'a plugin without a migrations descriptor is skipped' clause.

citations.anchor: passes each plugin its own folder and tracking table
citations.why: Asserts migrate() is called with that plugin's own `migrationsFolder` and its own `migrationsTable`, which is what makes plugins version independently.

citations.anchor: names the plugin, how far it got, and the order it depends on
citations.why: Matches the thrown message against /Migrating plugin "workspaces" failed — applied 2 of 4 plugin\(s\)/ and against /plugin ORDER/ — the plugin name, the committed count, the total and the ordering hint.

citations.anchor: keeps the original error as the cause
citations.why: Asserts the thrown error's `cause` is the original driver error ('relation "users" does not exist').

citations.anchor: does not attempt the plugins after it
citations.why: Asserts the plugin listed after the failing one never reaches migrate().
Asserts pool.end() ran exactly once after a plugin's migration threw — the failure half of the finally.

citations.anchor: closes the pool on success too
citations.why: Asserts pool.end() ran exactly once on a clean run — the success half.

citations.anchor: names host, port and database without the credentials
citations.why: Asserts describeTarget('postgresql://ortha:secret@localhost:5432/ortha_cms') is exactly 'localhost:5432/ortha_cms', so any credential in the target label fails it; the sibling case asserts the string does not contain 'secret'.

citations.anchor: says so rather than guessing when the URL will not parse
citations.why: Asserts an unparseable URL yields the literal '(unparseable DATABASE_URL)' rather than a guessed host/database.

citations.anchor: hands drizzle-kit an ephemeral config that never holds the credential
citations.why: Reads the temp config drizzle-kit was pointed at and asserts it contains 'process.env.DATABASE_URL' and neither the password nor the database name — the 'never written to disk' clause.

citations.anchor: passes the URL through the child
citations.why: Asserts the execFileSync options carry DATABASE_URL=<url> in the child's env — the 'passed through the environment' clause.

citations.anchor: cleans up the temp directory even when Studio fails
citations.why: Asserts the temp path no longer exists after drizzle-kit threw — the finally clause; the sibling case pins removal on a clean exit.

citations.anchor: warns, naming the exposure and how to undo it
citations.why: Asserts a console.warn for --host 0.0.0.0 containing the bound address '0.0.0.0:4983'; a sibling case asserts no warning for each loopback spelling. Only the 'prints a warning with the address' half is pinned — nothing asserts the warning precedes the drizzle-kit spawn, since execFileSync is a mock whose call order is not checked.

Asserts runDrizzleKitStudio does not throw when the child dies on SIGINT or SIGTERM, so studio's interrupt is a success. Pins only the studio third: dev and start settle through run.ts / superviseUntilExit, which have no test.

citations.anchor: passes a hostile --name as one literal argv element
citations.why: Asserts '--name=a b; rm -rf /' arrives as a single argv element and that the execFileSync options carry no `shell` property.

cli:I-22.reason: An absence claim about the whole package — 'the CLI reads no settings file of its own'. A test can assert what LAYOUT contains (packages/cli/src/lib/project.ts:25), but no harness can assert that nothing anywhere in the package ever reads a config file of its own; that is a review/grep property, not an assertion.
